content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm experiencing difficulties communicating via Modbus TCP/IP with the MBE - Powertool driver for Proficy Ifix SCADA. I've configured the [product_name] as a Modbus server and can read data using Modscan, but fail to transmit/receive successfully with MBE - Powertool. I've set up several GE controllers as Modbus servers without any issues on the client side. I'm wondering if the driver only works with GE controllers, although I haven't found documentation to confirm this. My client setup for the [product_name] matches that of the operational GE controllers. Any help would be appreciated.
Please note, not every [product_name] device is the same! Can you provide the exact [article_no]?
You have the newest [product_name] [version_no]. For this model, you need to enable both Modbus and S7 access.

Thanks! Checking the S7 access option resolved one part. However, there’s a new problem—transmits and receives function for a few minutes and then stop, even though data quality remains good. I have to reactivate the device on the client to resume communication.
Is your issue now completely resolved?
Not yet, I just updated my last response.
You edited your reply after I answered ...
Sorry for that. Do you have any idea why transmits and receives in MBE Powertool stop after a few minutes?
Unfortunately, I have no experience with MBE Powertool.
Has your [product_name] been updated to the latest firmware? [url]

analysis.insight_summary: The user is experiencing intermittent Modbus TCP/IP communication issues between a [product_name] and the MBE Powertool driver in Proficy Ifix SCADA. Initial setup and data reads are successful via Modscan, but data transmission ceases after a few minutes, requiring manual intervention to restore communication. This suggests possible compatibility or session persistence challenges, affecting overall reliability.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects stable and continuous Modbus TCP communication between the [product_name] and MBE Powertool, without needing to manually reset the connection. A similar level of interoperability as found with GE controllers is also anticipated.
